# Independent Adversarial Review — BGM Humanize It Creation Prompt

**Scope:** Read only `ENGINEERING-BRIEF.md`, `outputs/BGM-Humanize-It-Creation-Prompt.md`, and the four optional source files (humanize `SKILL.md`, `research.md`, `LICENSE`; skill-creator `SKILL.md`). I did not open `outputs/reviews/*` (prior review artifacts already present in the project) to keep this review independent, and did not access the web, MCP, or other chats. Where a finding rests on an external claim (a URL or paper result), I have not verified it myself — that remains the primary agent's or user's job, consistent with the Creation Prompt's own P8 requirement.

## 1. Semantic completeness — no material findings
I cross-checked every row of the Brief's "Mandatory audit decisions" table (lines 89–102), "Corrections to the merged prompt" (104–113), and "Useful installed Humanize guidance to retain" (115–121) against Creation Prompt P4–P7. Every row has a traceable, substantively equivalent treatment (sentence-quota rejection → P6 bullet 1; referent-consistency → P5.5; the genre table matches the Brief's five genres and Humanize's own five domain sections). Preference note, not a finding: the Brief (lines 87, 147) also calls for a separate coverage-matrix document. `outputs/reviews/` contains files that may serve this purpose, but I didn't open them, so I can't confirm — worth the primary agent checking, not a defect in the Creation Prompt itself.

## 2. Unsupported research claims — no material findings in the operative instructions
P1–P7 contain no bare empirical claims, unlike `humanize/SKILL.md`, which asserts uncaged figures ("AI uses [em dashes] at 3–5× the human rate", "87.88% average TPR reduction"). The Creation Prompt confines all such figures to P8's leads table, framed as questions/boundaries, and requires direct source inspection before any claim is used. P8 also extends coverage to leads present in `research.md` but absent from the Brief's curated table (DetectGPT/Fast-DetectGPT, PADBen, SilverSpeak, DAMAGE, RLCracker, De-mark, vendor roundups), correctly marking them unverified. I have not independently verified any cited URL or paper myself.

## 3. Source/sample separation — no material findings
P4's intake template keeps brief, source material, and samples distinct and explicitly neutralizes pasted content as non-authoritative. P5.8 and P9's V3/V13 cases directly exercise sample-fact leakage and embedded prompt injection.

## 4. Voice and genre preservation — no material findings
P6/P7 systematically rebut Humanize's rejected mechanisms (fragment/dash quotas, burstiness targets, Signal I pattern bans, forced creative-prose asymmetry) while explicitly preserving the rhetorical devices Humanize banned outright (anaphora, tricolons, chiasmus) when they serve purpose.

## 5. Construction versus runtime boundaries — no material findings
The boundary is stated three times consistently (P1, P6, P10), and the described runtime package (P3) carries no adversarial-review or Claude-review machinery into the shipped skill; P11 keeps construction reports out of runtime references.

## 6. Validation quality — two findings

**Finding A (Medium) — no negative/false-positive discovery test.**
- Evidence: P3 states "Ordinary proofreading, translation, code work, research-only questions and formatting-only operations do not need to become a full rewrite" — a discovery-discrimination requirement. P9's V1–V20 table only exercises cases where the skill *is* invoked; none test whether the drafted `description` actually avoids automatic-discovery selection for an excluded category.
- Failure case: the `description` ("Draft or revise prose for clarity, audience and authorial voice while preserving facts and the requested edit scope...") is broad enough to plausibly match a plain translation or proofreading request, silently converting a formatting-only task into a full rewrite — exactly what P3 says shouldn't happen — with nothing in P9 that would catch it before shipping.
- Correction: add a case (or extend V20) that submits an excluded-category request under automatic discovery and records whether the package is selected; unwanted selection is a failure requiring a tighter `description`.

**Finding B (Low) — validator-scope attribution is blurred.**
- Evidence: P9 says to run `quick_validate.py` and, in the same breath, "Check frontmatter, name/folder consistency, supported UI metadata, reference paths and their read conditions, absence of unfinished scaffold, reasonable entrypoint size and absence of unintended executable/dependency requirements." Skill-creator's own `SKILL.md` (lines 205–211) says the validator "checks frontmatter, naming, and unfinished scaffold placeholders" only.
- Failure case: a future constructing agent sees the script pass and treats UI metadata, reference wiring, and dependency checks as validated by that one command, skipping the manual inspection they actually need.
- Correction: split the sentence so it's unambiguous which checks come from the script output versus manual inspection.

## 7. Installation authority and coexistence — one finding

**Finding C (Medium-High) — default install root may not match the coexisting skills' actual discovery root.**
- Evidence: `humanize`/`ai-check` live at `/Users/damian/.agents/skills/...` (Brief 13–15; Creation Prompt P1 line 13). Skill-creator itself is installed at `/Users/damian/.codex/skills/.system/skill-creator/SKILL.md`, and its own default install guidance (line 151) is `$CODEX_HOME/skills` / `~/.codex/skills` — a different tree. Creation Prompt P11 adopts that same default without reconciling the mismatch.
- Failure case: a future agent follows P11 literally, installs `bgm-humanize-it` under `~/.codex/skills/`, and it is never discovered alongside `humanize`/`ai-check` at all — silently invalidating every coexistence guarantee in P1/P11 (selection-overlap disclosure, preserved automatic discovery) because the two packages are never loaded by the same mechanism.
- Correction: before defaulting to the skill-creator path, P11 should require confirming the actual discovery root(s) currently in effect (checking `CODEX_HOME`, any multi-root config, or whatever mechanism currently surfaces `humanize`/`ai-check`) and install wherever coexistence is actually meaningful, asking the user if the roots can't be reconciled. I haven't executed anything to confirm whether discovery already spans both roots — this may be a non-issue — so it's flagged as a verification requirement, not a confirmed defect.

## Summary
Semantic completeness, research-claim discipline, source/sample separation, voice/genre preservation, and construction/runtime separation show no material defects — the Creation Prompt is a faithful, well-hedged translation of the Brief, in places stronger than the Brief itself. The material findings are concentrated in validation coverage (missing negative-discovery test; blurred validator-scope description) and in installation/coexistence (unreconciled default-path mismatch against where Humanize actually lives). The primary agent owns any resulting edits.
